Not necessarily easy, but straight forward.

Gnocchi:

Boil potatoes for as long as you would for making mashed potatoes (usually 25 minutes for me if I cut them into thirds)

Drain and then run them through a potato ricer (a colander works too, I used that for a long time) and let cool for about 30-45 minutes.

Mix potatoes with 2 cups of flour per 1 pound of potato and salt (the dough should just be to the point where it's not sticky anymore). I honestly never measure the salt, so I couldn't tell you how much to add.

There are a couple of ways to roll out the dough. I've done both rolling out a sheet with some flour and a rolling pin (like you would cookie dough ready for cookie cutters) or rolling them between my hands to create a snake like you would Playdoh (I prefer the former).

Optional: use a fork to create ridges on top of the gnocchi dough, this can add texture and help them cook better, but it's not essential.

Cut the dough up into bit sized pieces and drop them into boiling water, be careful not to add too many at once of it'll cool the water too much and they won't cook properly. Remove them when they start to float, which should take about 2 minutes.

From here they're ready to eat, but there's any number of other things you can do as well. Such as pan frying them with butter and breadcrumbs or making a sauce to go with them (I think they work best with a cream sauce, but a red sauce works just as well).

They'll probably look terrible (even after years of doing it, mine never look that great), but anyone that has had frozen gnocchi will absolutely love them when they're fresh.

Chicken wings, you just put them in the oven for 45 minutes at 450. Put them on aluminum foil and make sure to drain the water from the pan after they thaw or they will never crisp up. Sauce em and good to go. (size of wing matters for time obviously and I like to flip them halfway and make sure they aren't sitting in juice for an even crisp on the skin)
